question: What type of energy does an MRI scanner use to produce diagnostic images?
explanation: MRI uses powerful magnets and radiofrequency waves rather than harmful radiation to create detailed pictures of the body. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is an MRI generally considered safer than a CT scan regarding radiation?

options.A: It exposes the body to much lower doses of standard X-rays
options.B: It completely avoids interacting with any atoms inside the human body
options.C: It requires the patient to take a protective oral medication first
options.D: It uses radiofrequency and magnetic fields instead of ionizing radiation

explanation: Spot on! Because an MRI doesn't use ionizing radiation, it's a much safer choice for avoiding radiation exposure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which part of the body is best seen using an MRI scan?
explanation: Great job! MRI is a star at showing soft tissues like muscles, tendons, and ligaments because they have a lot of water content. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h2)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a badly hurt knee and a suspected torn meniscus after a football match. Which test is the doctor most likely to order?
explanation: Well done! Knee cartilage and menisci are soft tissues, making an MRI the absolute best choice to check for tears. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which implanted medical device is a total no-go (absolute contraindication) for an MRI?
explanation: You got it! The strong magnet can mess up pacemaker settings, making it super dangerous for anyone with one to go near an MRI. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why must medicated skin patches that contain foil or metal be removed before an MRI?

options.A: The patch blocks all radiofrequency signals from the machine
options.B: The magnet will erase the chemical formula of the drug
options.C: The metal can cause skin burns from radiofrequency induction
options.D: The patch material will permanently stain the scanner tunnel

explanation: Correct! Metallic parts in patches can heat up super fast during the scan and burn the patient's skin. Safety first! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main reason nurses ask patients to take off all jewelry and hairpins before an MRI?

options.A: To keep the changing rooms clean and organized
options.B: To prevent static electricity from building up on clothing
options.C: To stop the patient from losing valuables during the test
options.D: To prevent metal objects from turning into dangerous projectiles

explanation: Spot on! That giant magnet can pull loose metal items like a flying bullet, which could hurt someone or break the machine. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h4)

question: A patient tells you they feel extremely panicked and short of breath at the thought of entering a narrow, enclosed scanner. What is your best first action?

options.A: Tell the patient to close their eyes and ignore the fear
options.B: Cancel the appointment permanently without consulting anyone
options.C: Force the patient into the scanner quickly to get it over with
options.D: Acknowledge the fear and report the need for an anti-anxiety medication order

explanation: You're a caring nurse! Validating their fear and helping arrange for medication or an open MRI makes the experience much better. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h4)

question: What protective item must be given to a patient before entering the MRI scanner to protect their ears?
explanation: Great! MRI machines make a loud knocking sound, so ear protection is a must to keep the patient comfortable. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is it so important for a patient to stay completely still during an MRI scan?

options.A: Shifting positions triggers an automatic safety alarm in the control room
options.B: Movement blurs the scan and ruins the quality of the pictures
options.C: Patient movement interferes with the electrical wiring of the hospital
options.D: Moving too fast can cause the machine's magnetic field to shut down

explanation: Spot on! Just like taking a photo with a phone camera, moving makes the image blurry and hard for doctors to read. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which rare, serious skin and tissue condition can develop in patients with bad kidney function who receive gadolinium contrast?
explanation: Well done! Gadolinium can trigger this serious condition in patients whose kidneys are struggling to filter waste. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is a key nursing duty right after a patient finishes an MRI where they received mild sedation?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake for the next twelve hours to prevent swelling
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk briskly around the unit to clear the drugs
options.C: Monitor vital signs and level of consciousness until the sedative wears off
options.D: Perform a complete neurological exam every five minutes for two hours

explanation: You got it! Keeping a close eye on vital signs and alertness helps ensure the patient safely recovers from the sedative. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h6)
